Ultimately, a framework for selecting image co-adding techniques is established, recommending either linear co-adding of images with identical point spread functions or of weights proportional to flux ratios, or the weighted median co-adding algorithm, which guarantees a well-defined point spread function in such cases.

Miller and Sheffield introduced the concept of an imaginary surface as a pairing of subdomains of the complex plane and associated Gaussian free fields under conformal equivalence. Specifically, they considered the relationship between these pairings and chordal Schramm-Loewner evolution. This paper develops that idea by exploring the relationship between imaginary surfaces and multiple SLEs driven by stochastic matrix models. We demonstrate the existence of a consistent imaginary surface family associated with these matrix models, such that the underlying subdomains and Gaussian free fields remain stable despite changes in scale and region. Additionally, we show that these pairings can be represented as combinations of conformally equivalent Gaussian free fields and simply connected regions. Specifically, we claim that these pairings are equivalent to combinations of independent Gaussian free fields and the imaginary part of a subdomain in the upper half-plane.

In this research, we address the Cauchy problem for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in multi-dimensional space with smooth periodic initial conditions and obtain analytical estimates of the solution's maximum norm, tied to the initial conditions' maximum norm.

The verification problem for quantum computation is crucial and challenging, where a quantum server attempts to convince a less computationally powerful classical client that a quantum circuit has produced a specific output. The fastest known protocol for verifying classical results in quantum computation has a time complexity of O(poly(κ)|C|^3), where κ is the soundness error and |C| is the size of the circuit. However, this can be overly expensive for complex circuits. We have developed a new interactive proof protocol that achieves a significant improvement, with a time complexity of O(poly(κ)|C|), making it more suitable for practical use for complex circuits.

Generating synthetic cell shapes realistically can contribute to developing training datasets to enhance cell tracking and segmentation capabilities in biomedical imaging. For effective cell shape synthesis, a compact yet flexible representation is required, however current methods involving voxel-based and polygon mesh approaches have limitations for modeling complex cell forms. Our research novelly applies implicit neural networks to represent cell shapes by utilizing a data-driven latent variable, its corresponding neural network, and corresponding occlusion mask. Our framework can synthesize high-resolution cell shapes according to a prior distribution defined by a large dataset of ground-truth cell shapes through occlusion ordering and region masking. Our method surpasses other techniques in synthesizing cell shapes with similar shape distribution and occlusion patterns as the input cell shape, while also producing shapes with similar material properties to real cells. Our code and generated cell shapes are publicly available at https://github.com/ukgib/cell-synthesis.

Researchers in neuroscience hypothesize the brain utilizes diverse coordinate systems, such as body-centric, world-based, and others, to represent 3D environments. Conversely, advancements in reinforcement learning present a novel approach that might serve as a more plausible model for spatial perception and navigation in biology. Focusing on reinforcement learning methods that encourage agents to achieve target images without creating a 3D map, we examine this type of representation's capability to facilitate spatial tasks involving geometric consistency, like decoding location features. The brain's retinal map is a 2D representation of 3D space; similarly, we investigate whether a 2D summary of visual data can support tasks requiring spatial coherence. Using generated synthetic images and target perceptions, we train agents to navigate 3D space successfully without maps, instead utilizing a 2D representation approximated through dimensionality reduction of visual features. The resulting agents excel at decoding location information from their visual representation, akin to the brain's retinal system. Our study demonstrates that a 2D representation can perform spatial tasks as well as 3D-based systems, presenting a more plausible model for biological spatial perception.

To evaluate the efficiency of event-chain Monte Carlo algorithms for complex simulations, specifically in two-dimensional models involving hard-disk dipoles bound together, researchers analyze the filling fraction of the search area and its relation to the reversibility of the underlying Markov process. By demonstrating varying filling fractions in non-reversible events, researchers diversify the event-chain method, offering an adaptable algorithm for achieving a balance between accuracy and efficiency.

The challenge of Sound Event Detection involves pinpointing the presence of specific sound events within an audio recording and indicating their exact location. Recently, researchers have made significant advancements in this area, thanks to the efficiency of Convolutional Recurrent Neural Networks. In this study, we present a novel CRNN model that uses 2D filters to analyze spatial patterns in stereo sound recordings, and through data augmentation by channel rotation, we increase the model's sensitivity to sound source locations. When tested on the Sound Event Detection task in the DCASE 2020 competition, our model demonstrated outstanding performance, ranking top 5 in both the development and the evaluation stages.

In traditional communication systems, signal interference is generally seen as detrimental, yet cutting-edge technologies have harnessed the power of superposition for simultaneous data transmission. By combining signals in accordance with recipients' capabilities, superposition coding (SC) maximizes information transfer and is nearly capacity-optimal. This comprehensive review delves into the fundamentals and applications of SC within the context of wireless communication. Beginning with an overview of SC's operational principles and performance assessment, the survey proceeds to examine various applications of SC in multi-user, multi-carrier, and deep space communication systems. Additionally, we discuss existing challenges and potential future directions for SC research.

Time-frequency analysis heavily relies on spectrograms, being a crucial component derived from the short time Fourier transform (STFT). These spectrograms comprise a collection of magnitude values, describing the time-frequency energy distributions of a signal, and thus embody significant importance for extracting relevant information. Existing signal analysis methodologies focusing on spectrogram values overlook the implicit spatial structure within these distributions, where higher energy is generally concentrated in narrower time-frequency bands. This study introduces novel geometric concepts to analyze spectrogram level sets, where a specified energy threshold is crossed, and its applications to signal detection and temporal synchronization are explored. By employing these new geometric notions, we devise detection algorithms that combine spatial statistics with machine learning techniques, and precisely align with the inherent structure of spectrogram level sets, thereby enhancing detection performance and accommodating varying sample sizes.

We present a novel universal method for detecting multiple types of dynamic behavior,
including stable and traveling chimera states using a dynamic network measure, a variant of
the direct communication approach. This method effectively pinpoints synchronized clusters
in networks of coupled phase oscillators and extensions of these networks, including those with
additive noise. Additionally, we demonstrate that a lower dimensionality of the attractor is
characterized by a higher number of negative eigenvalues obtained from the network's adjacency
matrix, specifically in cases of synchronized clusters. This methodology is employed to analyze
different network structures, including ring, chain, random, and small-world topologies with varying
degrees of connectivity. Results obtained from our method match those found using other detection
methods for chimeras and by numerically integrating the network equations. Furthermore, we use
this approach to analyze a model consisting of non-identical Kuramoto oscillators with and without
noise for different parameter values, as well as to observe the emergence of chimera patterns at the
level of a group of couples connecting to a common oscillator.

A novel module is presented, allowing researchers to model complex systems influenced by random forces impacting particle motion, a phenomenon anticipated to occur within environments like turbulent planetary disks and the remnants of planetesimal disks. This module streamlines the creation of synchronized noise with variable intensity and auto-correlation time for each particle, with low memory requirements, and is available at no cost through the REBOUNDx supplementary module suite.

Key aspects of quantum science include precise measurement and feedback mechanisms, yet current research mainly focuses on individual processes rather than combined measurement and feedback. To address this gap, this study proposes a master equation to analyze feedback mechanisms on a continuous scale. The proposed equation can simulate real-world scenarios by representing repeated measurements and adjustments and is versatile enough to be applied to various systems and controllers. Furthermore, this research demonstrates that solving this equation leads to Markov processes, which aligns with the principles of quantum feedback control as described in the original 1999 Katase and Arimitsu paper.

In a long and narrow container with horizontal base, two types of disks with varying sizes and weights are placed in an alternating sequence. This container is sealed by movable pistons which ensure all the disks come into contact with the container's wall when in a jammed state, resulting in a common power of the number of disks, (N^n), where 'n' equals either the number of larger disks or the number of smaller disks. This study focuses on a specific type of jammed configuration, specifically those with a high symmetry and a number of smaller disks that can be factored into a product of two integers. Jammed configurations with a high symmetry and a number of smaller disks that can be factored into a product of two integers also result in a common power of the number of disks, (N^2). Jammed configurations with a high symmetry and a number of smaller disks that can be factored into a product of two integers also result in a common power of the number of disks, (N^2).

Research into El Ni\~no's two main flavors - East Pacific and Central Pacific types - has become a significant focus in climate variability studies. Recent research aims to explore how these flavors affect global precipitation patterns, particularly in areas with low and high seasonal precipitation. Analysis of ENSO flavor-related precipitation patterns hasn't been extensively conducted, possibly due to limitations in identifying the flavor from monthly precipitation data. In this research, we identify the distinct spatial signatures of East Pacific and Central Pacific events, revealing that they are linked to distinct precipitation patterns in various Amazon regions, which are influenced by different atmospheric circulation responses. To confirm these findings, simulations from 29 climate models also show that they are consistent across distinct ENSO flavors.

Evidence suggesting the demographic characteristics of massive black holes is accumulating, spanning a broad spectrum of galaxy types, from large clusters to tiny dwarf galaxies. Despite this, the original paths of massive black holes remain shrouded in uncertainty. We have discovered a potentially significant indicator of massive black hole formation pathways in dwarf galaxies: the presence of a link between black hole mass and global stellar mass, but only in those with a mix of star-forming and metal-enriched populations, as seen in the dwarf galaxy Leo I. This indicator is absent in cluster galaxies and contradicts predictions made by simulations of massive black hole growth. The unique characteristics of Leo I, resembling the hypothesized properties of the hearts of primordial galaxies, prompts the hypothesis that a typical massive black hole formation pathway could appear similar to an EAGLE simulation's "merger-driven star-formation" scenario. This discovery calls for further exploration of simulation models, with a greater focus on the original paths of massive black holes, and encourages the continued observation of dwarf galaxies to distinguish between competing massive black hole formation theories.

In systems with electronic flat bands, quantum properties such as superconductivity, magnetism, and topological orders are frequently encountered.  Although the existence of flat bands is established in certain structures with geometric frustration like the kagome lattice, flat-band driven correlation effects are uncommon in such systems with multiple atomic orbitals.  In the study presented here, negative magnetoresistance and indicators of ferromagnetic fluctuations are discovered in a model kagome metal CoSn featuring a flat band at the Fermi level.  It was found that the flat band's influence hinders the transport of charge, and measures of its magnetic effects indicate that the system is on the threshold of magnetization or strong electron interaction.  These findings suggest that flat-band driven correlation effects can be a subtle driving force behind geometric frustration's unconventional quantum properties.

Understanding how genomic elements affect specific traits through genome-wide association studies remains complex due to the sheer number of available annotations. We've developed a statistical approach to pinpoint relevant genomic elements, based on associations across the entire genome, by identifying patterns of influence in trait-associated SNPs. This approach can incorporate multiple annotation types and has been successfully applied to eighteen human traits such as blood, platelet counts, metabolism-related disorders, height, obesity and a bowel disease, by examining 450 distinct genomic features across one hundred plus tissues and cells types. Our results show that protein-coding regions influence traits to a degree of up to twenty percent, in comparison with two percent, in a wide range of cases and highlight the significance of the capacity of different cells and tissues to translate genomic elements into a trait phenotype.

This study identifies and classifies 2-designs that satisfy specific conditions and have specific automorphism properties. A non-trivial 2-design's automorphism group can either be an instance of the previously documented examples described in this research or a specific subgroup within a larger group of automorphisms that corresponds to a geometric linear transformation involving a prime number.

This study examines electronic correlation within confined hydrogen, helium and lithium ions in their base states using entropy measures. Different wavefunctions are used to better account for inter-electronic interactions. The resulting entropy values show sensitivity to these interactions. In situations of extremely tight confinement, Coulomb effects are minimized and models treating particles as independent or non-interacting pairs in an impenetrable sphere are increasingly applicable. Energy estimates derived from these models align well with existing literature values.

The velocity distribution pattern of distant binary star systems in the galaxy should be the same regardless of their mass, rotation, and other characteristics, which can provide insight into gravitational physics. We propose a method to investigate this velocity pattern, specifically to look for potential anomalies, by analyzing the rotation curves of these binary star systems. By comparing their actual and predicted rotational velocities, we can search for signs of non-Newtonian gravitational behavior. If an anomaly is found, it is predicted to be a consistent underprediction of rotational velocities across the board, rather than an overprediction as seen in dark matter scenarios. This method offers a way to detect subtle deviations in gravitational forces on a galactic scale.

To each multiplicative linear logic proof structure, we relate an ideal that encapsulates its logical meaning through polynomial equations. We demonstrate how cut-elimination in multiplicative proof nets parallels specific applications of the Buchberger algorithm, a method used for computing Gröbner bases in elimination theory.

A sophisticated time series analysis technique called cross-correlation analysis has been developed to study complex time series systems, which are commonly seen in financial markets. This method examines the link between individual time series components within a system by creating a cross-reference plot of their temporal relationships, which effectively captures nonlinear interactions. To address the challenge of predicting time series states, our approach integrates cross-correlation analysis with machine learning, which utilizes the entropic properties of the obtained cross-plot trajectories. Experimental results demonstrate the feasibility of time series prediction using this method, specifically in the case of stock price movements.

THz radiation enables the precise stimulation of vibrational frequencies in molecules and crystals, leading to the introduction of inertial influences on electrons. By drawing a comparison to classical mechanics, where circular motion generates Coriolis and centrifugal forces, analogous effects arise, specifically spin-rotation coupling, centrifugal field coupling, and the interplay of these forces with the spin-orbit and the redshift of energy levels. These effects can persist for a few picoseconds following the initial stimulation, and potentially amplifying their magnitude could make this approach a promising means of controlling localized quantum states and chemical reaction barriers via vibration.

Current click-through rate (CTR) prediction models are largely dependent on behavior IDs that are based on past user-click history, but this approach has a significant limitation as it requires a certain amount of historical data for each behavior ID to function effectively. This constraint poses a major problem as it hampers the CTR prediction for new ads without sufficient historical data. To overcome this issue, our approach involves employing ad visual content information to enhance the CTR prediction performance for new ads. Firstly, an improved neural network is developed that integrates the visual content information from multiple ads into the learning framework, thereby allowing for the representation of ads with limited historical data. Secondly, an embedding network is proposed to embed visual content information that is complementary to behavior IDs. Thirdly, a dual-ranking model is combined with the enhanced ads embedding information to boost the CTR prediction performance. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms the baseline method, delivering a 2.44% absolute improvement in CTR prediction accuracy for new ads and a 0.58% absolute improvement in overall CTR prediction accuracy.

Traditionally, business process management concentrated on organized, task-based processes, but the rise in importance of intellectual work necessitates a more comprehensive approach, encompassing processes that rely on unstructured activities, often accompanied by sizable document collections.  Aligned with the emerging trend towards incorporating formal concepts into business process management, this research introduces a refined version of current case management paradigms, enabling the representation of document collections with specified cardinalities as part of business processes.  The proposed approach is based on a process semantics comprising states, operations, and process instances, with the added feature of cardinality constraints.  A related logic for specifying properties related to the enforcement of processes is defined, with a focus on the relationship between these process specifications and the specified cardinalities.  The outcomes of this research include a method to transfer property specifications to process models and, conversely, a method to derive such specifications from process models, with evidence gathered through the analysis of an actual use case in the healthcare sector.

Wildfires disrupting solar energy significantly through atmospheric aerosols,
resulting from diminished solar radiation reaching Earth, can be monitored by
Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) data streams retrieved from geostationary satellites.
These data streams are susceptible to gaps and discrepancies due to cloud
obstructions, satellite calibration issues, and spatial sampling limitations.
Therefore, predicting AOD values accurately by filling in the gaps and refining
existing readings is essential for applying machine learning and deep learning
techniques in wildfire forecasting. By incorporating physical laws and initial
satellite readings into a multi-source dataset, a diverse set of features can be
generated, enabling the training of models to fill in the gaps and refine the
readings. Specifically, Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and Long Short-Term Memory
(LSTM) models were tried and tested on Aerosol Optical Depth data streams from
the Suomi NPP MODIS and VIIRS satellites. Ultimately, the LSTM model performed
best, outshining other temporal and deep learning models by producing highly
correlated predicted AOD values and achieving superior physics-informed
error metrics with a remarkable 85% reduction in Mean Absolute Error (MAE) for
most wildfire events. These improvements have far-reaching implications for using
satellite data streams in wildfire modeling and forecasting.

Protecting users of location-based services with significant privacy requirements is extremely difficult when multiple locations are shared within a short time frame due to the significant relationships anticipated between these locations. Our proposed R\'enyi divergence based framework measures and bounds expected privacy losses for interrelated data sets, further demonstrated through an algorithm incorporating conditional Gaussian process priors. This framework illustrates the challenges in safeguarding dependent data and provides a strategic approach to maintaining sensitive location data privacy within a specified boundary.

Research has shown that combining resting-state functional MRI data from multiple sites can potentially introduce systematic biases in connectivity measures. In this research, we studied how site-to-site effects impact our ability to detect individual and group differences, and our analysis suggests that multisite studies are feasible when utilizing large sample sizes. Our data collection was based on 100 subjects with two sites and 100 participants per site, resulting in a total of 200 subjects. By applying multisite and single-site analysis methods to our data, we observed that site-to-site effects did not significantly impact our ability to detect individual and group differences, and our results reveal that group effects were highly significant. Our findings also suggest that single-site and multisite datasets yield comparable effects, and our data suggests that multisite analyses can be an attractive option for researchers.

Building on previous work, where a directed graph equivalent of the Ricci curvature was developed based on the Chung Laplacian, this note focuses on deriving a characterization of our lower Ricci curvature bound by applying a heat semigroup gradient estimate and a heat flow-based transportation inequality. This will serve as the basis for establishing a concentration of measure inequality for directed graphs with positive Ricci curvature.

Recent advances in NLP for code-mixed texts have gained considerable attention, 
mainly driven by the widespread use of language blending in social media across 
multi-lingual countries such as India, Mexico, Europe, and parts of the USA. 
Given their importance, improving processing efficiency and accuracy for code- 
mixed texts has become a pressing research need. Current models represent 
character-level positional encoding based on a pre-defined script order, 
ignoring the dynamic switching patterns inherent to language mixing. This paper 
introduces PESTO (POSEitional encoding for TOngues), a novel encoder that 
addresses this limitation by leveraging the inherent properties of language 
blending. PESTO employs relative position encoding specific to individual 
languages, integrated with encoding for language ID. This innovative design 
facilitates dynamic encoding adjustments according to the script order used in 
language blending. PESTO outperforms state-of-the-art models on language 
mixing datasets from Sanskrit-based languages (Hindi-Urdu) and Latin-based 
languages (Spanish), as well as from single languages (Hindi). The code and 
models can be accessed at https://github.com/sonu9570/PESTO.

Using a combination of density functional calculations and the linearized Migdal-Eliashberg equations with the functional derivative approach, we analyzed how the density of states affects the isotope effect and critical temperature of the H3S hydride superconductor at various pressures. We found that accounting for the variable density of states significantly improves the match with experimental data for the pressure-dependent critical temperature. Additionally, we confirmed that the phonon-mediated pairing in this material occurs through a combination of hydrogen vibrations with low and high energies. Our results provide a thorough explanation for the observed behavior and offer a framework for future research into the properties of superconducting H3S.

Fisher developed the Fundamental Theorem of Natural Selection by combining the concepts of population increase and evolutionary change, and in doing so, introduced a crucial distinction between average and overall effects. Within the framework of causal models, this distinction can be characterized through the integration of a functional cause with a probability distribution over possible effects, and understanding this concept resolves a long-standing debate regarding the correct application of selection dynamics in evolutionary theory.

This paper will present our approach to optimizing bipedal robot walking assisted by thrusters using a closed-loop feedback system. By assuming that supervisory controllers are properly set, we will concentrate on refining joint trajectories to meet specific performance requirements. To achieve this, we will create a mediator filter to separate the tasks of thruster-assisted walking and generate compatible joint trajectories. This approach is demonstrated to be effective through simulations on a quadruped robot powered by mini-thrusters and the results show significant improvements in walking efficiency and robustness under various conditions.

This research proposes a visual relocalization technique based on geometric information derived from 3D surfel mapping. A comprehensive database of images is initially created, linking 2D image features to 3D geometric entities via global indices obtained through mapping rendering. By applying surfel mapping's native rendering capabilities, this method achieves precise linkages between image features and 3D entities without resorting to additional constraints. Moreover, a method is developed to obtain learned descriptors for each image feature from a given 3D map, leveraging surfel normals and poses to derive beneficial insights. By utilizing these descriptors, the relocalization process can effectively identify and weigh potential 3D entities associated with each image feature's description. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in both geometric and learning-based 3D visual relocalization domains.

Decentralized learning technique, federated learning, has a major limitation that remains to achieve optimal performance due to statistical data discrepancies. Overcoming this issue, researchers have focused on personalizing machine learning models, which typically rely on having complete datasets, an unrealistic scenario given data labeling complexities. When models receive limited labeling, they experience reduced adaptability to local distributions and, subsequently, suffer performance degradation. Addressing this issue, we propose an innovative approach where under-resourced clients collaborate with data-rich proxies by engaging in semi-supervised learning. The goal is to minimize uncertainty in annotations provided by the proxy, which proves to be a critical adaptation challenge. Moreover, we devise a novel metric to measure proxy reliability based on proxy uncertainty and confidence, ultimately leading to the development of FSSLA, a personalized FSLS method utilizing optimal proxy confidence for reliable results. The effectiveness of our method is demonstrated through comprehensive experiments where it outperforms current methods, specifically showing significant improvements of up to 26.5% in test accuracy on ResNet-18 using MNIST and up to 15.6% on ResNet-50 when evaluating on CIFAR-10 using VGG-16.

Simulations of second-long black hole-neutron star mergers in numerical relativity are conducted to obtain a comprehensive picture of the inspiral, merger, and post-merger stages.  The analysis across various initial and computational configurations reveals universally similar evolution processes, regardless of setup variations.  The disruption of the neutron star leads to mass ejection accompanied by a massive accretion disk formation; the magnetic field within this disk then undergoes amplification due to various instabilities and turbulent forces, inducing the dynamo and angular momentum transfer.  The subsequent mass ejection by viscous magnetohydrodynamic turbulence begins roughly 300-500 milliseconds post-merger, persists for several hundred milliseconds; meanwhile, a magnetosphere is formed around the black hole, producing a focused strong electromagnetic outflow lasting about 0.5-2 seconds.  The model without equatorial-plane symmetry shows inverted magnetic polarity due to a magnetorotational instability dynamo, caused by the initial configuration's magnetic field strength and the type of equation of state it adheres to also influences the resulting mass ejection and magnetosphere properties.

A novel variation of the Kawazumi-Zhang invariant, specifically $\varphi(C)$,
for compact Riemann surfaces $C$ of genus $g \geq 1$ is presented, exploring
its connections to the first Mumford-Morita-Miller class $e_1 = \kappa_1$ on the
moduli space and its relation to the traditional Kawazumi-Zhang invariant.

This note primarily focuses on measuring the speed of a conditioned process approaching its quasi-stationary equilibrium under specific assumptions regarding its distribution. In reverse, we establish that a conditioned process converging uniformly to a self-conservative, ergodic Markov process also attains a distinct quasi-stationary equilibrium, which it converges toward at an exponential rate across all initial distributions. Furthermore, we illustrate a corollary ergodic theorem under specific conditions.

This research explores the optical interaction between a dimer of dielectric nanoparticles near a graphene layer. By applying a precise electromagnetic model, we computed the optical force acting on each particle and derived equations to assess the influence of graphene's surface plasmons. Our findings demonstrate that the excitation of graphene's surface plasmons can produce numerous stable positions with interparticle distances much shorter than the wavelength. Additionally, we found that these positions can be dynamically manipulated by adjusting the graphene's chemical potential. Both perpendicular and angled light incidence have been taken into account in the study.

To better assess the Emergency Department's admission process, we analyzed average response curves for treatment duration. Extending the time for treatment is considered an effective strategy for improving admissions; nonetheless, empirical evidence supporting this claim is difficult to gather. The treatment duration is impacted by various unmeasurable patient factors and coincides with the admission decision, which are challenging variables to manipulate. We depicted the admission process as a complex network, which revealed that the average response curves cannot be determined without nonparametric modeling due to confounding factors influencing patient health. We therefore adopted a parametric model, incorporating an unobserved patient health variable, to analyze data from a large hospital treating abdominal pain patients (28,862 patients). Our study found that shortening the Emergency Department treatment time to two hours decreases admissions by nearly nine percentage points and expanding the time by half an hour minimizes admissions without noticeably altering readmission and revisit rates.

Coordination of tasks among multiple robots can be achieved through various strategies, but we examine a specific scenario in which a central control unit makes decisions for the robots. Our study focuses on a network where robots are equally spaced and connected to a central control via a regular lattice structure, with each node except the center having two connected neighbors. We investigate the capacity of this lattice to coordinate tasks efficiently and determine the optimal method for distributing tasks when the robots' movement patterns are random and independent of each other. We then derive an algorithm that achieves near-optimal performance and allow the robots to adaptively make decisions without requiring prior knowledge of the task distribution. Finally, we confirm through simulation the results of our theoretical analysis.

Research has examined the correlations of charges in particle interactions within Pb-Pb collisions, specifically looking at whether evidence exists for the Chiral Magnetic Effect (CME). The study focused on specific signal indicators: the directed flow of charges and their differences, and the quadrupole arrangements of charges. It analyzed these relationships in collisions at 2.76 and 5.02 TeV, while also accounting for an background influence related to an anisotropic particle flow. The results suggest that contributions from the CME do not exceed 7% of the observed influence related to the directed flow of charges and their differences, and contributed negligibly to the quadrupole arrangements of charges. The study's findings set a limit on the CME influence related to the directed flow of charges and their differences, with an upper bound of 1-14 nmrad per unit of magnetic field strength.

The surge in online fundraising (or "crowdfunding") research focuses on understanding the crowd dynamics that predict the success of crowdfunded projects. Differing from prior studies that concentrated on project characteristics, our analysis takes a more holistic approach and is less dependent on the specific crowdfunding platforms being used. By combining various research methods, we explored the impact of features describing crowd behavior on project success. Through a multi-platform investigation of fundraising in online markets, our findings reveal the common crowd dynamics that indicate success across the spectrum of crowdfunding platforms.

Machine learning (ML) based detection of network attacks has shown effectiveness when tailored to a single organisation, but combining data from multiple sources is challenging due to data format inconsistencies and privacy concerns. To address this issue, this paper introduces a collaborative federated learning framework, allowing multiple organisations to co-create and train a robust ML-based intrusion detection system without compromising their data's privacy. A key feature of the proposed framework is the ability to collect and process network traffic data in a common format to demonstrate the efficacy of distributed training. Furthermore, the study compares this approach with traditional training methods and finds that federated learning yields comparable accuracy results.

A novel algorithm is introduced to tackle the challenge of sequencing multi-point robotic manipulator tasks, aiming to minimize overall assembly time and accommodate a high level of task complexity without significant additional computational costs. Key features of the proposed algorithm include an initial assessment phase, a clustering phase, and a time-table construction phase, all of which contribute to efficient performance. By comparing the algorithm to a classic method on a case study involving the assembly of a CW567K aircraft part, evidence shows that the proposed solution outperforms the standard approach with notably reduced computational costs, indicating its potential to improve real-world applications in the aerospace industry.

The performance of the interface between semiconductors and barriers is a crucial factor in producing consistent, high-quality quantum dots essential for reliable quantum information processing. This research investigates the characteristics of undoped Si substrates by measuring SiMOSFET Hall bars, thereby evaluating the quality of fully fabricated CMOS devices. A notable mobility level of 800 cm^2/Vs was achieved with a gate length of 30 nm, showcasing a superior interface suitable for integrating quantum dots into advanced digital circuits.

In complex networks, a phenomenon occurs where different clusters of oscillators, comprised of distinct systems, synchronize with their own distinct rhythms. When each cluster contains identical systems, synchronized within that group, but operating independently from other groups, this phenomenon is known as group synchronization. Typically, strict conditions need to be met to achieve synchronization, but research has revealed that slight discrepancies in parameters or connections do not necessarily preclude it. Through advanced analysis, it is now possible to identify stable conditions for group synchronization, including the impact of within-group connections. This expanded understanding allows for a more general representation of these complex systems, reducing their stability evaluation to simpler mathematical dimensions.

Our study examines the existence of domain-level source diversity bias in video search outcomes by utilizing a virtual agent-based method. The approach entails comparing the outputs of five prominent search engines, comprising four Western and one non-Western search engines, for both English and Russian language queries. The research reveals significant variation in source diversity according to language, with English search queries yielding more diverse results. Additionally, the analysis discovers that the video-sharing platform YouTube dominates the top search outputs for all Western search engines, except Google. Interestingly, the sampled Google search results lack video content from its main competitors, including Vimeo and Dailymotion, implying a possible ranking bias towards Google-owned YouTube. These findings underscore the need for further investigations into own-content bias within Google's search outcomes.

To gain insight into supersymmetric monodromy defects in the critical Wess-Zumino model, researchers utilize analytical bootstrapping techniques, beginning with a precursor investigation of related systems that are also intriguing in their own right. These precursor studies involve the analysis of two key systems: monodromy defects without supersymmetry, and a Wess-Zumino model with a defect-free ε-expansion. Building on existing research regarding codimension-two conformal blocks and Lorentzian inversion formulas, the monodromy defects study extends its reach to include parity-odd structures, offering a deeper understanding. Meanwhile, the ε-expansion study focuses on bootstrapping four-point functions of chiral operators in the Wess-Zumino model, aiming to provide key spectral information about the model's underlying theory. Following these foundational investigations, the analysis proceeds to two-point functions of chiral operators in the presence of a supersymmetric monodromy defect. The resulting expressions for these two-point functions are expressed through novel, in-depth special functions analysis. Notably, the techniques employed and discoveries made here are versatile and likely applicable to diverse other theoretical frameworks.

We prove that there is exactly one elliptic curve, up to uniqueness, defined over a cubic Galois field extension of rational numbers with a point on the curve having an order of 13 that is rational in the extension and that curve is not defined by the rational numbers.

This paper explores the interplay between interference correlation and randomness in wireless networks, highlighting their combined impact on interference events and network performance. A detailed analysis of interference correlation in Gaussian networks is presented, followed by a comprehensive study of its effects in networks with variable power levels and splitting ratios. Our findings indicate that increasing randomness can either mitigate or exacerbate interference correlation, thereby influencing the optimal trade-off between correlation and randomness. Furthermore, this research offers a framework for evaluating the potential benefits of splitting times and power levels, with potential applications in wireless networks managing interference correlation.

Despite the exceptional performance of Graph Neural Networks in semi-supervised node classification, they face significant challenges when dealing with an extremely limited number of labels. The semi-supervised pseudo-labeling method is often employed to mitigate this issue, which aims to supplement the training set with high-confidence, pseudo-labeled nodes in a self-training cycle. Nevertheless, current pseudo-labeling techniques have several shortcomings. Primarily, they expand the label set cautiously by choosing only the most confident, yet potentially uninformative nodes, which merely shift the labeling burden to the next iteration. Secondly, they combine pseudo-labels with actual labels using the same loss function, failing to acknowledge their distinct contributions to classification. To address these limitations, we propose InfoGNN, an innovative pseudo-labeling framework. InfoGNN focuses on labeling nodes with the greatest informative value, which effectively counters data scarcity. Theoretical justifications for its superiority are provided, along with experimental results demonstrating its advantages over state-of-the-art baselines on four benchmark datasets.

In video processing tasks, precisely identifying key frames is essential for effective analysis. Traditional methods, which are often based on optical flow or feature matching, can be too computationally expensive for real-time applications. This is particularly problematic when using modern high-frame-rate cameras. To address this limitation, we introduce PatchNet, a rapid keyframe detection algorithm that leverages patch-level similarity comparison to calculate an optimal matching field. By utilizing a patch-based network instead of average pooling, we significantly improve detection accuracy while maintaining low computational requirements. Notably, PatchNet achieves a 40x speedup over state-of-the-art feature-based methods while demonstrating a 10% increase in ground-truth similarity.

We examine the one-dimensional discrete-time asymmetric exclusion process with periodic boundary conditions, using a variety of different initial conditions. These initial conditions are characterized by a complex, multi-variant distribution function. We derive algebraic expressions for the distribution function, which reveals a subtle interplay of conservation laws depending on the specific initial conditions employed. Additionally, the periodic boundary conditions introduce unique characteristics to the system, resulting in a verification of the conjectured phase transitions outlined in Lahela and Jarvenpaa's 2018 study.

A new method of efficient wireless communication is proposed in a novel SWIPT system, enabling faster and more sustainable mobile data networks. The system, utilizing energy-harvesting technology from access points without the need for a splitter, allocates part of the frequency spectrum for information transmission and the remaining for energy capture. To analyze performance improvements, an optimization problem was created that maximizes energy gain and maintains a minimum data rate in a multi-user OFDMA network. Next, the challenge of concurrent information transmission and energy harvesting was evaluated through Monte Carlo simulations, demonstrating improved energy efficiency and data reliability.

In Fermi gases with low concentrations of magnetic properties, a particular phenomenon occurs at specific points beyond the applicability of second-order approximations in mathematical modeling. To address this issue, researchers revisited third-order approximations for systems with multiple magnetic components and developed expressions incorporating both gas concentration and magnetic alignment parameters. These new expressions align with computer-simulated predictions for both concentrated and magnetically aligned scenarios. Furthermore, the model's terms were linked to fundamental concepts in physics, and the correction factors were analyzed in various magnetic alignment scenarios. Lastly, the model's implications for the critical temperature in superfluid phase transitions were explored.

We present a generic, classical modeling of electric circuits to describe conventional single-tone microwave optomechanics, where a mechanical oscillator functions as a mobile capacitor within a parallel RLC circuit. Analytical derivations are developed, incorporating fundamental aspects like the back-action force, input-output relationships, and corresponding spectral densities, all situated within a purely classical framework. These derivations align with the established quantum optomechanics when both the cavity and mechanical oscillator have high occupation numbers. Additionally, the derived analysis equates to the existing quantum treatment in this specific context.

Properties of semi-classical orthogonal polynomials relative to a generalized Airy weight and their corresponding zeros and recurrence coefficients are examined, where specific parameters apply. The study extends to a symmetrized form of this weight known as the generalized sextic Freud weight, resulting in a parallel investigation of the associated polynomials' properties.

This study investigates how basic robot movements can suddenly shift from predictable to chaotic behavior when following a wall in a featureless environment. We're looking into how these transitions occur and what causes them to happen. Our analysis shows that two different types of movement, a straight line and an arc, can lead to these chaotic transitions. We've found that attracting cycles, which occur when the robot moves in a perfect pattern, can suddenly become unstable and lead to chaotic motion when the robot's starting position is slightly off. This happens because even tiny changes in the robot's initial position can significantly affect its movement, making it go in different directions. This discovery is similar to phenomena observed in other complex systems, such as weather patterns and electrical signals in the brain.

This article further explores and develops the concept of chiral aspects in 2dcft within the pAQFT framework, building upon a previously published study.  It specifically investigates how these aspects relate to a massless scalar field in globally hyperbolic 2-dimensional spacetimes.  The study identifies subalgebras that contain either chiral or anti-chiral observables, constructing these explicitly and showing they are embedded in the full theory's algebra.  It also establishes that the construction of these subalgebras is Cauchy surface-independent and yields a well-defined covariant theory on the space of null geodesics.

Laparoscopic surgery has limitations due to the partial visibility of organ structures, which is a critical concern during operations. To counteract this issue, researchers have developed smoke reduction technologies to improve visibility, but their methods often fail to address the underlying problem. To this end, a smoke detection algorithm primarily aims to identify and evaluate the extent of smoke presence in surgical videos. However, current smoke detection algorithms are restricted to a single task and can't simultaneously perform smoke detection and reduce the negative impact of haze and smoke from images. In this research, a deep learning-based smoke detection model is introduced, which not only effectively identifies smoke in surgical videos but also beneficially affects the reduction of haze and smoke from images, ultimately improving the visibility of organ structures in surgical videos. To this end, a multi-task network is proposed, which integrates smoke detection and atmospheric filter modules. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed model, a multi-task smoke detection dataset consisting of three tasks, including smoke detection, defogging, and image super-resolution, was created and used in experiments. The results show that the proposed model outperforms single-task models, demonstrating its superiority.

This research focuses on creating resilient Molmer-Sorensen gates using trapped ions arranged in a line, incorporating Gaussian amplitude modulation and a consistent laser frequency. We chose a frequency that maintains balanced entanglement accumulation across all motion modes to provide a significant degree of protection against frequency errors, particularly for long chains of ions. A demonstration of this method is performed on a chain of three ions, achieving an average reduction of under one percent from peak precision within a twenty kilohertz range of frequency deviation, and the efficiency of this gate design is assessed through numerical simulations on chains consisting of two to thirty-three ions.

Using advanced computer simulations of atoms in motion, we've found that titanium in barium titanate maintains an unexpected position within its molecular structure even when it's not polarized. This finding challenges the common assumption used to model this phase. To address this discrepancy, we performed a thorough analysis of the symmetries at play and created a series of more accurate, detailed models that capture the underlying structure of the material. From these, we identified the smallest models that are stable and consistent with experimental data; these models also predict a critical temperature that matches the one observed in experiments. Additionally, we used these models to simulate how barium titanate might change when it's subjected to different voltages, and our results show that like a similar material, strontium titanate, barium titanate is likely nonpolar even when it's not in its usual polar state.

Multivariate data that change over space or time can often be analyzed with a statistical model known as multivariate Gaussian processes (GP). Researchers have developed new methods to analyze these data by combining them with a statistical model known as Gaussian graphical models (GGMs). By combining the two models, researchers can analyze relationships within the data while accounting for its functional nature. A mathematical framework has been developed to represent these combined models, which relies on the concept of graphically defined GP. This new framework has been applied to the analysis of functional data from a fertility study and real-life environmental scenarios.

Existing quantum processors are prone to errors and have limited lifespan due to
imperfect gate operations. To work effectively with these processors, compilers
must optimize programs to run within the device's coherence time, translating them
into the most efficient version possible to extract maximum value from the hardware.
We have developed new, deterministic methods to efficiently compile repetitive quantum
circuits within a short period of time. Specifically, these patterns are found in
circuits that use the variational quantum eigensolver to study molecular systems and
RyRz variational quantum solver. We've demonstrated that our pattern-based approach
can significantly reduce compilation time, up to 30 times faster than the standard
compilation method in certain cases. This optimized compilation also yields an
average 10% decrease in circuit depth and a 31% decrease in gate count for a
specific quantum chemistry application.

A recent approach to optimizing techniques employs average-case analysis, enabling more nuanced convergence speed declarations than conventional worst-case results, yet these faster declarations are only applicable to models with limited data availability. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel concept known as average-case universality, allowing for broader generalizations of optimization methods. Specifically, we demonstrate that for convex losses and Euclidean data, average-case results for first-order methods translate to convergence rates based on the worst-case data distribution, thereby encompassing the traditional worst-case regime. Furthermore, we introduce a related notion called robustness, which guarantees that optimization methods remain effective in the presence of perturbed data. We formally define average-case robustness and establish its relationship with average-case results. Leveraging these concepts, we systematically evaluate the average-case robustness of four distinct optimization methods, including gradient descent, Nesterov's acceleration, Fenchel-Duick method, and Stochastic Scaled Gradient Method. Our findings showcase the complexity of optimizing techniques in average-case settings, yet also highlight instances of robustness and universally applicable methods, thereby contributing to a more comprehensive understanding of optimization dynamics.

Recent breakthroughs in producing two-dimensional materials with specific patterns of layered structures have paved the way for achieving unique states known as excitonic insulators, in which certain inherent electronic characteristics spontaneously emerge within the layers. A novel concept has been introduced where two layers comprised of different semiconducting and superconducting materials can coexist, giving rise to unprecedented polaronic excitations at their interface. Researchers have developed a theoretical framework to model these excitations by applying a rigorous mathematical techniques to solve complex interactions between inherent layer electrons and those resulting from interfacial electron transfers. The outcome predicts distinct spectral changes within the interfacial electron spectrum when the two layers transition from a normal to a superconducting state, and these modifications occur at specific energy levels corresponding to the formation of bound electron-hole pairs. The model also predicts the appearance of canted layers at a specific energy level corresponding to the formation of these bound pairs, and the model also predicts the rapid decay of these bound pairs within these canted layers.

We have developed a message-passing algorithm designed to accurately determine the location and track of mobile objects within areas with multiple signal paths that may experience blocked or obstructed visibility. The proposed adaptive probabilistic algorithm estimates a mobile device's location by leveraging data from multiple anchors, taking into account the timing and amplitude variations in signal components and associated uncertainties. Utilizing an adaptable noise model, the algorithm enables accurate estimation of the agent's position, even without precise knowledge of the surrounding environment. The algorithm dynamically adjusts its operation in real-time according to changes in signal strength and the likelihood of direct line-of-sight visibility with each anchor. Numerical testing demonstrates that the algorithm remains effective in areas with intense signal interference and temporary obstructions.

Measurements of joint polarization states for $W$ and $Z$ bosons in $W^{\pm}Z$ production processes have been reported. These measurements were derived from $139$ fb$^{-1}$ worth of data from proton-proton collisions at a $13$ TeV center-of-mass energy, obtained with the ATLAS detector at CERN's Large Hadron Collider.  $W^{\pm}Z$ candidate events, resulting from the decay of these bosons into electrons and muons, have been used to quantify longitudinally polarized vector boson pair production, an event that is rarely observed but crucial for verifying the Standard Model's predictions.  Multiple polarization state combinations have been analyzed, and observed results align with Standard Model forecasts across multiple production mechanisms.  These measurements represent the most sensitive tests to date of the ratio between gauge boson polarization and its transverse momentum.  A notable increase in sensitivity has also been achieved in searching for a neutral natural doublet Higgs boson, a task that will continue to contribute significantly to verification of the Standard Model and potential beyond-the-Standard-Model theories.

Research indicates that the Cotton tensor offers a more comprehensive understanding of gravity, particularly in four-dimensional spacetimes, as it is less influenced by volume changes and more sensitive to local gravitational effects. Furthermore, the Cotton tensor can be calculated using a young tableaux method, which simplifies its computation compared to other formulations. Although the Cotton tensor's solutions may appear diverse and less intuitive than General Relativity, its unique features and numerous equivalent forms demonstrate the diversity of information it contains about spacetime geometry. The Cotton tensor's field equations can also be expressed in several mathematically equivalent forms that highlight their geometric significance in terms of conformal metrics, Hodge duals, and Schouten-Nijenhuis differentials. These forms reveal the connections between the Cotton tensor's curvature-based definition and more abstract, cohomological properties of spacetime geometry.

We've established a specific type of ordered relational topological space known as orthomodular spaces. Our method for creating these spaces involves combining a particular kind of frame, introduced by Hartonas, with a topology in a manner similar to the approach taken by Goldblatt and then extended by Bimbó, in relation to the representation theory of ortholattices. The orthomodular lattices and their corresponding homomorphisms can be shown to have a dual equivalence to the orthomodular spaces and their respective continuous morphisms.

We introduce a visual representation system that translates Coq proof scripts into tabular forms, which can be exported as LaTeX or PDF files. Our tool aims to facilitate learning and proof review by making it easier to comprehend proof scripts, especially for novice users. Additionally, we outline several future research opportunities and highlight our own approach to addressing these challenges.

We demonstrate that the fourth moment of holomorphic Hecke cusp forms is limited under the assumption of the Riemann Hypothesis for a specific degree 8 L-function. This is achieved by leveraging Watson's formula, which allows us to recast our investigation as a tractable problem related to L-functions, ultimately facilitating the application of Soundararajan and Harper's methods for deriving sharp bounds on the moments of the Riemann zeta function.

In interior point methods (IPMs), where an iterative method is employed to solve a linear equation system, speeding up convergence often involves developing optimal preconditioners for the linear solver. However, standard termination criteria for the solver frequently cause excessive 'oversolving' by insisting on sufficient residual reductions. This paper presents an alternative approach to interior point methods that involves modifying the interior point mechanism to enable earlier termination of the linear solver once a sufficient inner objective function reduction is achieved, without compromising IPM convergence properties. We demonstrate that with this modification, Krylov solvers can be terminated sooner, and present strategies for determining optimal inner iteration limits based on an inner objective function tolerance, leading to considerable time savings in practical tests without sacrificing convergence rates.

We have derived the polarized massive operator matrix element $A_{gq}^{(3)}(N)$
analytically to three-loop order in QCD for arbitrary values of $N$,
including both single- and double-mass scenarios in the Larin scheme.
Furthermore, the result serves as a crucial transition function for the variable
flavor number scheme at $O(\alpha_s^3)$ and is also expressed in momentum
space for convenient use.

Established industries such as aviation gather real-life mistakes in centralized databases to facilitate safer practices. Conversely, emerging technologies like intelligent systems frequently result in real-world setbacks despite a lack of comprehensive record of their incidents. Consequence: similar technical issues (e.g. biased algorithms, false positives) cause repeated failures in the intelligent systems field. Our solution: creating a database of actual incidents (i.e. the AI Incident Database). The database at present contains 268 instances which have been analyzed to reveal underlying problems and their corresponding technical roots. It has also provided pointers for preventing future incidents. The database and research findings are accessible to the public for inspiration.

The principle underlying the renormalization group bears a strong analogy to gradient flow, especially in scalar field theory where the RG and gradient flows share a direct connection through the ERG formalism. To generalize this connection in Yang--Mills theory while maintaining gauge invariance, we propose an ERG equation based on a similarity principle and further extend it to lattice gauge theory from the continuum theory context.

Business processes are becoming more complex, thus there's a need for them to be modeled as compositions of basic activities, governed by strict rules to ensure consistency. Research has been conducted to analyze these processes using the concept of monitoring, allowing for the creation of dynamic business process models with a direct relationship to executable code. This work presents a method for creating complex business process models by combining flow elements with conflict resolution mechanisms, drawing inspiration from hybrid automata. These hybrid automata, when integrated with additional monitoring tools, can effectively check dynamic business process models for inconsistencies, providing a solid foundation for future business process model analysis and monitoring techniques.

Quipper, a domain-specific language, enables the description of quantum circuits by embedding in Haskell, resulting in a highly functional and practical language. Yet, its embedded nature in Haskell hinders the development of a formal semantics, limiting the definition of a tailored abstract machine. The absence of a formal semantics complicates the detection and resolution of performance issues. To bridge this gap, we define a formal semantics for Quipper-M, a quantum circuit description language, based on a typed logical framework. Additionally, we design an abstract machine modelled after the Berlin Abstract Machine, specifically adapted for the typed logical framework of Quipper-M.

We establish a scaling relationship near a critical point in a finite system governed by random matrix theory. The behavior we're studying is related to the largest eigenvalue of a random matrix, and it exhibits a complex transition as the size of the system changes. By analyzing the fluctuations surrounding this critical point, we find that they can be described using a universal distribution that applies across various types of critical behavior. The largest of these fluctuations grows rapidly as the system size increases, and it influences the behavior of the largest eigenvalue. We use numerical simulations to verify our findings and explore how they're impacted by the addition of an external factor that drives the system towards this critical point.

We suggest creating bosonic pairs using large numbers of dipoles with complex internal structures, which are coupled to a cavity through radiation. By leveraging quantum vacuum fluctuations and non-linear interactions within the cavity, we can produce pairs of dipoles in the ground state of both the cavity and the dipoles. To achieve this, we'll analyze the balance between pair production and squeezing of the cavity mode, and explore how to optimize this process for optical phase measurements. We'll also consider the impact of external driving and discuss the potential benefits of using dipoles with three-level Lambda or E-prime configurations.

Assembling a complete genome from short, overlapping DNA sequences is a critical yet computationally complex task within genomics. Due to the rapidly expanding genomic dataset, high-performance and scalable approaches are essential for managing the increased computational demands. A novel, parallel algorithm is proposed to generate continuous DNA sequences from the overlap graph of a genome, leveraging graph partitioning and island-based assembly concepts. By isolating and solving the overlap graph's optimal sequence problem for each partition, the algorithm yields continuous sequences with high overall sequence quality. Without relying on a parallel in-silico assembly framework, our method demonstrates superior performance and high sequence quality, outperforming existing approaches in distributed-computation assembly of large genomes.

A modified logistic equation, previously known as Hutchinson's or Wright's equation, originally aimed to model oscillating ecological phenomena. However, it received criticism from mathematicians for being based on an unstable process called "density dependent feeding behavior." This feedback mechanism was considered unfeasible from a biological perspective. We introduce an equation that addresses this criticism and allows for the analysis of global dynamics in a low-dimensional model. Despite being a simple logistic equation with a one period delay, its properties are not fully understood and are subject to significant uncertainty.

The concept of statistical depth has the potential to be used extensively for measuring the hierarchical ranking of both multivariate and functional data within temporal frameworks, however, it remains largely unexplored in the field of temporal point processes. Recent research has developed a point process depth by incorporating a weighted product of two terms - one representing the depth of process magnitude, and the other describing the temporal occurrence of events given that magnitude. The second component is challenging due to the complex nature of event timings and thus far, methods like Gaussian and Dirichlet distributions have been used despite these distributions failing to capture the true underlying patterns of event frequencies. In order to address this issue, a new method called the Isometric Log-Ratio (ILR) transformation is proposed, allowing the calculation of event frequencies across intervals within any fixed process magnitude. The ILR transformation shares some similarities with techniques previously used to analyze multivariate data within functional contexts, and it also possesses some unique properties such as monotonicity and the ability to be differentiated. The ILR transformation can also effectively identify underlying patterns of event frequencies within simulated data, and it also accurately differentiates between significantly ranked processes in both simulated and real-world data when compared to alternative techniques like time-warped prioritization. The ILR transformation is now made available through an open-source library called R package called pdepth.

Achieving maximum engine performance involves leveraging quantum effects. In this investigation, two strategies for enhancing engine performance are explored, both of which guarantee optimal performance in various scenarios. The initial approach involves using a hybrid quantum machine that combines quantum and classical components, which can reach thermodynamic limits when in contact with multiple energy sources. When interacting with a single energy source, this machine attains optimal performance equivalent to that of quantum turbines and refrigerators. The second strategy employs quantum machines with limited availability of relevant inputs, which can reach thermodynamic limits when in contact with a single energy source. The guarantees provided by these strategies enable the attainment of thermodynamic limits in various scenarios.

Researchers employed a precise laser spectroscopy method on three isotopes of germanium at the ISOLDE-CERN facility to study their hyperfine properties. The measurements involved a highly accurate laser source with a 269 nm wavelength, generated through a combination of techniques. The study included state-of-the-art theoretical calculations that enabled researchers to determine the nuclear quadrupole moments and precise magnetic properties of these isotopes.

Researchers have introduced an innovative technique for accurately measuring the masses of extremely short-lived, unusual atomic isotopes over a wide range of frequencies. This method utilizes the principle of isochronous mass spectrometry, combining real-time ion velocity and trajectory analysis at the Lanzhou CSRe particle storage facility. Dubbed Bρ-defined isochronous mass spectrometry, or Bρ-IMS, this technique enhances precision and sensitivity, paving the way for new mass measurements. Specifically, in a single test setting, precise mass readings were obtained for $^{46}$Cr, $^{50}$Fe, and $^{54}$Ni with exceptionally low margins of error. This breakthrough technique will serve as a crucial tool for evaluating the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa quark interaction matrix and for further refining the measurements of highly rare atomic isotopes.

This tutorial notebook exemplifies a novel technique for generating Boltzmann distributions of lattice field theories through normalizing flows, a subset of machine learning models. The underlying concepts presented in papers arXiv:1904.12072, arXiv:2002.02428, and arXiv:2003.06413 are summarized, accompanied by a detailed, concrete implementation of this approach. The tutorial showcases its application in a lattice scalar field theory and U(1) gauge theory contexts, which particularly incorporates gauge symmetries into its flow-based method for the latter. The tutorial's interactive format is best experienced with the associated Jupyter notebook, which we highly recommend utilizing.

We aim to enhance the accuracy of structured text recognition by incorporating predefined formats defined through regular expressions, thereby facilitating the identification of specific patterns. Our method, involving a Weighted Finite-State Transducer model, boosts recognition accuracy on targeted formats, with minimal losses in other instances. A key parameter governs the intensity of the formatting influence. The proposed technique finds applications in text analysis, particularly when dealing with formatted documents, where recognizing numerical and alphabetical sequences with specific separators can be crucial. For instance, extracting phone numbers or addresses from unstructured text using regular expressions can significantly aid this task. Although our approach's primary objective is to improve structured text recognition, it also possesses secondary utility in targeted extraction tasks.

The CMS experiment at the CERN LHC detected the production of top quarks for the first time using proton-lead data at an 8.16 TeV nucleon-nucleon center-of-mass energy. Top quark production was identified in events featuring one isolated electron or muon and four or more jets, from a data set totaling 174.5/nucleon/pair. The experiment's researchers compared the measured signal to predictions from the standard model and the results support the expected rates of top quark production in such events. Additionally, upper limits on top quark production were calculated in proton-lead collisions with the hypothesis that the top quarks originate from protons. The new findings narrow the range of a protons' density by a factor of 22.3 over 0-0.48 pseudorapidity coverage or 5.9 over 0.48-4.00 pseudorapidity coverage.

This study focuses on key elements in cross-domain text-to-SQL parsing, specifically schema linking and value filling. To enhance encoding abilities, a column selection auxiliary task is proposed, leveraging explicit targets for relevance matching. Additionally, two value filling approaches are presented to bridge the gap between current zero-shot parsers and practical applications, considering that many existing parsers overlook value filling in synthesized SQL. Experiments on the Spider dataset demonstrate the superiority of our proposed framework over state-of-the-art models in all three areas, further validating the advantages of our framework over a prominent zero-shot parser, with notable improvements in execution accuracy and query validity.

The ongoing LoTSS survey is conducting a thorough observation of the Northern sky to better understand how the large-scale structure of the Universe changes and develops. Although only 1% of the sky is covered in the LoTSS DR1 data release, analysis shows fluctuations that need to be understood. To address these issues, mock catalogues are created to predict potential sources of error and galaxy clustering patterns in the LoTSS data are studied. The study also employs an advanced analysis technique to identify and eliminate small-scale noise, resulting in two different methods to correct and smooth the data. After applying these corrections, analysis of the LoTSS data shows that the galaxy distribution in the data matches the expected smooth, cosmic pattern on large scales. The study further employs multiple techniques to measure the relationship between galaxy distribution and the distribution of the underlying dark matter, confirming previous findings on this topic. Based on these analyses, estimates of galaxy biasing and dark matter density variations in the LoTSS area are measured, revealing a mild discrepancy with previous measurements that may be attributed to the limited, current data coverage. The study demonstrates that the LoTSS survey is effective in addressing these questions and the forthcoming, upcoming data will allow for even more precise research.

The High-Dimensional Rank Lasso (HDR Lasso) model offers a computationally efficient solution to handle complex data analysis. Introduced as a parameter-free and robust method for high-dimensional settings, the HDR Lasso has been proven to outperform other methods in statistical accuracy. Mathematically, the HDR Lasso can be formulated as an optimization problem with an l1-regularized loss function. Due to its robustness, the HDR Lasso has numerous applications in fields such as economics, finance, and machine learning. Despite its advantages, the HDR Lasso has been challenging to solve, and existing solutions have been prone to getting stuck in local optima or taking an excessively long time to converge, especially for large datasets. In this study, a new adaptive sieving algorithm called AS2 has been proposed to tackle the HDR Lasso. Based on an initial guess from an active-set algorithm called SPGL1, AS2 selectively refines relevant features, and repeatedly updates and refines subsets of active features, simultaneously solving sub-problems and eliminating inactive ones. AS2's implementation has been backed by an extensive convergence theorem and empirical results demonstrating its superior performance to alternative methods, particularly in achieving higher accuracy and reducing computational time. Additionally, the researchers have conducted thorough examinations of AS2's properties using synthetic and real-world datasets, and the algorithm has been made available for public use.

We have proven that in the slow driving limit, the average rate at which the second law's violation exceeds a certain threshold is always minimized when a system reaches a state of maximum entropy production among all possible stationary states. This optimized rate can be expressed as the sum of two components - one resulting from the system's deviation from optimal entropy production and another resulting from the system's velocity under influence. This optimized rate can also be achieved in the fast driving limit through detailed calculations for specific models, such as a particle bonding with a heat bath and a particle bouncing off a wall with randomness. Furthermore, our research has shown that in the fast driving limit, the system's average rate of entropy production is always proportional to the system's average driving force and is unaffected by the system's memory duration.

Over the past decade, significant advancements in artificial intelligence have positioned it as a key tool for addressing environmental concerns, primarily reducing greenhouse gas emissions. However, researchers have lately come to recognize that increasingly complex AI models require substantial amounts of energy to train, thereby contributing to the very emissions they are intended to mitigate. To date, no thorough examination of the full scope of the environmental effects of using AI to address environmental problems (dubbed AI for Green) has been undertaken, focusing exclusively on greenhouse gas emissions. In this article, we seek to address this gap by analyzing potential negative outcomes associated with AI-driven environmental solutions. Initially, we will categorize and analyze various types of AI's environmental impacts. Subsequently, we will present established methods for evaluating these impacts, illustrate how they can be quantified and compared across different applications. Ultimately, we will suggest novel directions for future research within the AI for Green domain.

This paper examines prescriptive process monitoring, which proactively issues warnings or takes corrective actions to prevent process issues from arising.
